supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40:23 UTC, PowerShell ran on WS-ZADAMS-01 as ian.doyle with the command `-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \\FILE-SUN-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1`; Sysmon and Windows process-creation telemetry corroborate the execution.

The activity aligns with the documented IT patching practice: ian.doyle remotely runs that same patch script from WS-IDOYLE-01, and workstation patching was scheduled during business hours. The preceding network logon identifies ian.doyle and WS-IDOYLE-01 as the source.

The PowerShell process connected to the explicit proxy, which recorded a successful Windows Update download of about 38.8 MB; PowerShell then launched wusa to install a Windows update package in quiet, no-restart mode.
The wusa and PowerShell processes exited shortly afterward, consistent with the brief window reported by the user.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records show the PowerShell command line and related process and network activity, but do not include the contents, hash, or signature verification of Patch-Workstations.ps1 or the downloaded update package.
The records do not establish everything the script may have done beyond the observed process and network events.
claims_not_established: The available evidence does not independently verify the integrity or contents of Patch-Workstations.ps1.
The available evidence does not establish whether any activity outside the supplied records occurred.
unrelated_findings: Separate ticket: FILE-SUN-01 (10.55.20.20) made an RDP connection to WS-ZADAMS-01 at 13:41 UTC.
